explain.say: Inside a spider's abdomen are silk glands. An orb-weaving spider can have up to seven kinds, each making a different silk, for safety lines, sticky spirals or egg sacs.

faq.q: Why do spiders make different kinds of silk?
faq.a: Each gland makes silk for a job: tough dragline for safety ropes and web frames, stretchy sticky silk for catching prey, soft silk for wrapping eggs. An orb weaver can make up to seven kinds.
asks: How many types of silk can a spider make?

faq.q: Is spider silk liquid inside the spider?
faq.a: Yes. Silk is stored as a concentrated liquid of protein called dope. It only turns into a solid thread as it is drawn through the duct and pulled out of the spinnerets.
asks: How does liquid silk become a thread?

faq.q: What makes spider silk so strong?
faq.a: In the duct, stretching lines up the long protein chains. Some parts lock into hard crystals for strength, while other parts stay springy and tangled for stretch, so the thread is both strong and tough.
asks: What is spider silk made of?

faq.a: Spinnerets are small, movable nozzles at the tip of a spider's abdomen. Each has many tiny spigots, and the spider can combine threads from several to make thicker or sticky lines.
asks: Where does silk come out of a spider?
How many spinnerets do spiders have?

faq.q: Do spiders run out of silk?
faq.a: Silk is made of protein, which costs food to make. Many orb weavers eat their old web each day and recycle the protein into fresh silk.
asks: Why do spiders eat their webs?
Can a spider run out of web?

facts: Spider silk is stored as a liquid protein solution and becomes solid as it is drawn through the spinning duct.
Female orb-weaving spiders can have up to seven types of silk gland.

quiz.why: The spider draws silk out of the spinnerets; the pulling helps the proteins line up into a strong thread.
